band_strategies.description: Control: approximate equal thirds by predicted need.
Very concentrated product hypothesis: top 5%, next 15%, rest.
Concentrated product hypothesis: top 10%, next 20%, rest.
Moderately concentrated product hypothesis: top 15%, next 25%, rest.
Broad top-heavy product hypothesis: top 20%, next 30%, rest.
Wide high-priority hypothesis: top 25%, next 25%, rest.

limitations: this report can guide the next LLM allocation hypothesis but cannot promote runtime policy

methodology.band_strategy: Sort families by ranking score, preserve ties, then apply explicit top-heavy cut fractions. Equal tertiles are kept as the control.
methodology.candidate_pool_policy: Default run evaluates the strongest formula scopes from the existing formula sweep ordering plus the accepted candidate. Pass --formula-scope-limit 0 for an exhaustive formula matrix.
methodology.normalization_boundary: This still uses the repaired product-scope case surface, so missing case-type mass is reported and not silently imputed.
methodology.primary_grade: Primary ordering uses base_product_prior measured-only failure. The top-heavy grade emphasizes high_need minus rest failure rate, then multiplies by monotonic high>=middle>=low order and measured target coverage.
methodology.purpose: Check whether semantic-veto evidence need is better represented by a concentrated top slice than by equal thirds, and whether source-exposure weighting surfaces product-important daily-language families.

ranking_modes.description: Control: use the formula score directly.
Product-impact hypothesis: a hard rare family may matter less than a moderately hard common family.
Light exposure weighting while mostly preserving algorithmic need.
Balanced need/exposure ranking for the daily-language concentration hypothesis.

next_steps: Compare accepted-candidate equal-tertile rows against top-heavy source-exposure rows.
If top-heavy rows concentrate failure and generated-evidence lift, use top-N budget curves for allocation instead of thirds.
Keep low and middle controls in the next generation batch so the concentrated-ranking hypothesis remains falsifiable.
